put.description: Creates a new HorizonDB cluster or replaces an existing cluster. PointInTimeRestore creates the new Cluster resource and hydrates its service-owned database storage from an available source backup. It does not clone source pools, Pool-scoped endpoints, firewall rules, parameter-group associations, or other child resources. The new Cluster receives its service-generated Cluster-scoped Endpoint named cluster. PostgreSQL version is inherited from backup metadata; all other new-cluster configuration comes from the request or service defaults. Until cross-region point-in-time restore is supported, the target cluster location must match the source cluster location; a cross-region request is rejected synchronously with 400 CrossRegionPointInTimeRestoreNotSupported and does not create or modify a resource.

patch.description: Updates the service-created Microsoft Entra authentication method. State Enabled enables the feature and State Disabled disables it; no additional properties are required. Disabling the feature does not remove or modify database roles or users previously created through the MicrosoftEntraAdministrators control-plane API or directly through pgaadauth extension functions. The method may be Disabled even when password authentication is also Disabled.

get.description: Gets the service-created PostgreSQL username-and-password authentication method.

parameters.name: clusterName
parameters.description: The name of the HorizonDB cluster.

patch.description: Updates the service-created PostgreSQL username-and-password authentication method. The request is sparse and omitted properties preserve their current values. A state-only request enables or disables the authentication mechanism; disabling cannot include credentials and does not remove or modify existing database users or roles. Login-only, password-only, and combined credential updates require this method to already be Enabled unless this request also sets state to Enabled. PostgreSQL is the sole source of truth; the control plane stores no administrator identity or credentials. The service bootstraps an AzureSU-owned special group, only AzureSU can grant or revoke its membership, and at most one user role can be a member. Login-only or password-only updates require exactly one current member. A combined administratorLogin and administratorLoginPassword request creates and adds a new user when no member exists, resets the password when the member name matches, or renames the member and resets its password when names differ. A requested name that already exists outside the special group is rejected to prevent privilege elevation. Both authentication methods may be Disabled.

postgreSqlVersion.description: The PostgreSQL major version used by the HorizonDB cluster. API version 2026-09-01 accepts only 17. This property is required on every PUT and is immutable after creation. On replacement, resubmitting 17 is accepted and any other value is rejected. For point-in-time restore, PostgreSQL version is the only new-cluster property inherited from the source backup metadata, and the value in the request must match that version. All other new-cluster configuration comes from the request or service defaults.

creationMode.description: The mode used to create the cluster. When this property is omitted while creating a new cluster, the service records Create. PointInTimeRestore creates a new cluster from an available backup; pointInTimeUtc and creationSourceClusterResourceId are then required, postgreSqlVersion must match the source backup's major version, and the target cluster location must match the source cluster location until cross-region point-in-time restore is supported. This property is immutable and is returned as creation provenance. On replacement, omission preserves the recorded value, resubmitting the same value is accepted, and changing it is rejected.

pointInTimeUtc.description: The requested point in time, in UTC, to restore from. This property is required when creationMode is PointInTimeRestore and must be absent for other creation modes or when creationMode is omitted. The service honors this value for same-region restore. Until cross-region point-in-time restore is supported, the target cluster location must match the source cluster location; a cross-region request is rejected synchronously with 400 CrossRegionPointInTimeRestoreNotSupported and does not create or modify a resource. This property can only be specified during resource creation.

creationSourceClusterResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the source HorizonDB cluster used by the selected creation mode. This property is required for PointInTimeRestore and other source-based creation modes, and must be absent when creationMode is Create or omitted. Until cross-region point-in-time restore is supported, PointInTimeRestore requires the target and source clusters to be in the same Azure region. A source cluster does not need to have a pool to be restored, provided an available backup exists. This immutable creation-provenance value does not change after creation.

PasswordAuthenticationPropertiesForPatch.description: Properties for updating PostgreSQL username-and-password authentication. Omitted properties preserve their current values. State-only requests enable or disable the authentication mechanism. Credentials are secrets and are never returned or stored by the control plane. Login-only, password-only, and combined credential updates require this authentication method to already be Enabled unless the request also sets state to Enabled.

state.description: The target password-authentication state. Enabled or Disabled can be supplied without credentials to toggle the feature. Disabled cannot be combined with administratorLogin or administratorLoginPassword. Disabling password authentication does not remove or modify existing database users or roles.

administratorLogin.description: The PostgreSQL administrator role name. A login-only update requires password authentication to already be Enabled unless state is set to Enabled in this request, and requires exactly one member in the AzureSU-owned special group. The current name is an idempotent no-op; a different name renames the current member only when that target role does not already exist. When supplied together with administratorLoginPassword, this value can create the administrator if the special group has no member, reset the matching member's password, or rename a differently named member and reset its password.

administratorLoginPassword.description: The PostgreSQL administrator password. A password-only update requires password authentication to already be Enabled unless state is set to Enabled in this request, and requires exactly one member in the AzureSU-owned special group. When supplied together with administratorLogin, it can create the administrator if the special group has no member, reset the matching member's password, or rename a differently named member and reset its password.

ReadWritePoolProperties.description: The current designated read-write pool and read-write status for a HorizonDB cluster. When a pool is created while the cluster currently has no pools, the service automatically designates the new pool as the read-write pool. This behavior also applies after all pools that existed earlier in the cluster's lifetime have been deleted.

designatedPoolResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the pool designated to host the cluster's read-write node. The pool is a child resource of this cluster. When a pool is created while the cluster currently has no pools, the service automatically sets this property to the new pool's resource ID, including when all pools that existed earlier in the cluster's lifetime were deleted. This property is absent when no pool is designated.

failover.description: The current failover status for the read-write node. This object is always returned on reads. When failover is not ready, state is NotReady and unavailableReason explains why.

zoneRedundancy.description: The current zone redundancy status for the read-write node. This object is always returned on reads. When zone redundancy is not ready, state is NotReady and unavailableReason explains why.

state.description: The current zone-redundancy readiness state for the read-write node. The state is NotReady when no read-write pool is designated.

unavailableReason.description: The reason zone redundancy is not ready. This property is present only when state is NotReady and absent when state is Ready. Valid reasons are that no read-write pool is designated, the designated read-write pool has fewer than two nodes, all nodes in the designated read-write pool are deployed in a single availability zone, or the region does not support availability zones.

ZoneRedundancyState.description: The readiness state for zone redundancy of the read-write node.

values.description: Zone redundancy is not ready. Inspect unavailableReason for details.
